name: ScamRead cyber news feed
note: Headlines and summaries are written by AI (Claude) from the original reports. Follow the source links for the full articles.

items.headline: Drupal Warns of Highly Critical Core Flaw Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: Drupal has warned that a new highly critical site takeover flaw in its core is being exploited in the wild. It is tracked as CVE-2026-136716 and is related to the earlier Fail2Install issue, addressing remaining vulnerable installation states.

concept.title: What is a software flaw that attackers exploit?
points: A software flaw is a mistake in a program's code that lets a stranger do things they should not be allowed to do, like a weak lock.
Attackers find the flaw, then send a specially built request that uses it to take control of the website, such as changing its pages.
Website owners should install updates from the software maker as soon as they are released, since an update (a fix from the maker) closes the flaw.

items.headline: CISA Adds Ten Exploited Flaws Including Danfoss and Mitel Products
items.summary: CISA added ten vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after evidence of active attacks. Affected products include Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers, HPE Juniper Session Smart routers and Mitel MiCollab.

concept.title: What is an exploited vulnerability?
points: A vulnerability is a weakness in software or a device, like a door that does not lock properly, which can let an outsider get in.
An exploited flaw means attackers are already using a method to take advantage of that weakness, so a government cyber agency adds it to a public list.
Owners of affected devices should install the maker's fix (a software update that closes the weakness) as soon as it is available.

items.headline: Critical Drupal Fail2Install Flaw Added to CISA Exploited List
items.summary: CISA added a critical remote code execution flaw in Drupal core, tracked as CVE-2026-132165, to its exploited vulnerabilities catalog. Federal agencies must apply fixes by November 27, 2026.

concept.title: What is a remote code execution flaw?
points: A software flaw is a mistake in a program's code that attackers can use to cause harm. A remote code execution flaw lets an attacker run their own commands on a computer from far away over the internet.
Attackers scan for unpatched systems and use the flaw to take control of the website or server without needing a password.
Software makers release patches (fixes for known flaws), so installing updates quickly is one of the simplest ways to stay protected.

items.headline: Hackers Exploited Fortinet Flaws in Commercial Ship Networks, US Probes
items.summary: US authorities are investigating whether Iran was behind attacks on Fortinet FortiGate devices that may have compromised up to 50 commercial ships. The count is an intelligence estimate and attribution is unconfirmed.

concept.title: What does it mean to exploit a security flaw?
points: A security flaw is a mistake in software that works like a hidden gap in a lock.
Attackers scan the internet for devices with the flaw, then send special messages that let them enter without permission.
Installing the maker's fix (called a patch) as soon as it is released closes the gap before attackers can use it.

items.headline: 1Password Customer Data Stolen After Employee GitHub Account Breach
items.summary: 1Password disclosed that an attacker hijacked an employee's corporate GitHub account and used it to push malicious code to backend services. The intrusion was used to steal customer data.

concept.title: What is an account takeover?
points: An account takeover is when a criminal gets into someone else's login, like using a stolen key to enter a locked office.
The attacker may steal a password or a login token (a small code that keeps someone signed in), then use the trusted account to reach private data.
Companies can protect staff accounts by using two-step login, which asks for a second code from a phone.
